criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First three sentences name the asserter (Governor Dunleavy), restate the claim, and signal the correction ('The tense is wrong') without snark. Fractional deduction because the hook paraphrases the claim rather than quoting it verbatim.

criteria.name: Claim load-bearing + AK stakes
criteria.notes: Governor's CS Education Week proclamation directly governs DEED CS-education grant framing statewide. Correction names three concrete actor categories, dollar amounts ($1B+ BEAD, $629M awarded), agencies, and a 2025-2028 deployment window with a 30% coverage gap.

criteria.name: Steelman fairness
criteria.notes: Paragraph two states the strongest honest version generously: real $1B+ BEAD funding, 29 projects, remote tech work genuine and growing, premise sound. No snark. Reader feels fairly represented before the rebuttal.

criteria.name: Counter-evidence quality
criteria.notes: Primary rebuttal rests on Commerce Commissioner Julie Sande's Juneau Empire op-ed (state primary). BroadbandNow/FCC 68.5% figure is credible secondary but is_primary false and a single outlet, short of the two-independent-outlet bar for a 10.

criteria.name: Factual density
criteria.notes: Specifics every 1-2 sentences: dates, dollar amounts, subgrantee counts, 46,000 homes, 70%, Utqiagvik to Metlakatla, 68.5%, 25/3 Mbps, 2025-2028 timeline.

criteria.name: Source quality
criteria.notes: Claim attribution traces to the Governor's proclamation and DEED page (primary). Main counter (Sande/Juneau Empire) is primary. BroadbandNow is FCC-derived secondary, one outlet, preventing a clean 10. All sources present in claim_dossier.json.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Matches examples/post_001.md: analytical, structural, position-taking, corrective without contempt. Minor deduction for 'So here's the open question.'

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Tight 2-4 sentence paragraphs, one 3-item bullet block, ~435 words, ~2922 chars, easy to scan.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Real, debatable binary tied to the corrected sequencing frame. No 'follow us', no rhetorical softener.

criteria.name: Business actionability
criteria.notes: Reader can identify their category from the three named actors and name the concrete decision to reframe during the 2025-2028 BEAD window.

hard_fail_checks.hashtag_count_in_range: PASS — 4 hashtags, within 3-5, all at post end, none inline
hard_fail_checks.punctuation_bans_held: PASS — zero em/en/double-hyphen, colon, or semicolon in body; single hyphens only as list markers and compound adjectives
hard_fail_checks.claim_is_attributed: PASS — names Governor Mike Dunleavy and quotes the claim verbatim, traces to selected_claim.asserters[0]
hard_fail_checks.steelman_present: PASS — genuine steelman in paragraph two before the rebuttal

one_sentence_fix: Supplement the BroadbandNow 68.5% statistic with a second independent credible source (e.g. FCC Form 477 state-level data or an NTIA BEAD coverage map citation) so every rebuttal point rests on two independent credible outlets.
